facts.fact: The World Bank project paper states that the open-source social protection MIS Ke-Non, deployed in 2024, is integrated with the Unique Social Registry, which holds socio-demographic data on 8,740 families (about 16 percent of the population), and that the MIS tracks beneficiaries, services and payments.
facts.system: Ke-Non (CORE-MIS/openIMIS) integrated with the Unique Social Registry

systems.owner: DPSSF, Ministry of Labor, Solidarity and Social Security
Government of Sao Tome and Principe

note: Fact dated by the document's publication date; it gives no date for the integration itself. The document does not say that two or more programmes draw on the USR, and states the digital ID linkage only as an intended synergy.
